newsitem.title: USA: INCSTAR says 1996 hurt by radioimmunoassay erosion.
newsitem.headline: INCSTAR says 1996 hurt by radioimmunoassay erosion.

text.p: INCSTAR Corp said 1996 financial results "reflect a continued erosion of our radioimmunoassay product offerings."

"We continue to make the necessary investments in research and product development that have already begun shifting the mix of our product sales away from RIA tests to non-isotopic formats," said chief executive John Booth.
For the year, INCSTAR said sales declined three percent to $44.3 million in 1996 from $45.8 million in 1995. Profits for 1996 were $4.1 million, down from $4.3 million.

For the fourth quarter, sales fell eight percent to $10.9 million from $11.9 million in the prior year. Quarterly profits fell to $848,000 from $1.5 million, said the developer and maker of medical and clinical tests.

On January 24, INCSTAR said it signed a memorandum of understanding to be acquired by a unit of American Standard Cos Inc in a one-step cash transaction. Each INCSTAR common share would be converted to the right to receive $6.32 in cash, under the agreement.

Closing of the proposed merger is conditioned on the simultaneous closing of a previously announced sale by Sorin Biomedica SpA, INCSTAR's majority shareholder, of its European Diagnostics Division to American Standard.
The proposed merger is subject to negotiation and execution of mutually satisfactory definitive documentation and other conditions, INCSTAR said.
